figures.alt: Wide low-slope roof with drains, tapered crickets, membrane seams, and parapet scuppers
figures.caption: A coating or replacement decision starts with the roof assembly as it exists: drainage, seams, penetrations, flashings, substrate condition, and the route water takes across the field.
figures.before: The Assessment: What Has to Happen Before You Make the Decision

figures.alt: Flashed metal roof scupper with clean membrane and small dry leaf accumulation
figures.caption: Coating can be appropriate only when the existing assembly and drainage details can be prepared, repaired, and protected without masking a larger failure.

figures.alt: Low-slope parapet with primary scupper and separate higher emergency-overflow scupper
figures.caption: Replacement is warranted when the roof system cannot reliably manage water through the field, perimeter, penetrations, and primary and emergency drainage paths.
